display.purpose: Page titles, hero headlines, sheet titles. Tight negative letter-spacing carries the editorial signal.

headline.purpose: Section headers inside dense screens, card titles.

label.purpose: Section captions, group labels, form labels. The 14% tracking is the system's rhythm.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: Default boundary on outline buttons, input chrome, and any element that needs to be present without being framed.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: The paper-card resting elevation. Whisper, not lift.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Popovers and floating menus. The lift moment.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: Hover focus aura on primary actions.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: BottomSheet upward-facing elevation when the sheet hovers above the page.

motion.name: editorial-ease
motion.purpose: The project's universal exponential ease-out curve. Used by all sheet/drawer transitions, page enters, and list staggers.

motion.name: sheet-spring
motion.purpose: BottomSheet open motion. Snappy without bounce.

motion.name: popover-duration
motion.purpose: Default duration for popovers and quick fades.

narrative.overview:
JobFlex's interface is a workshop that has been kept. Organized, a little beautiful, ready for the next job. Type and whitespace carry the weight; color is a tool, not a uniform. The aesthetic family is small-shop editorial: Cabin, Sutro, Mast, the early Stripe blog era. Magazine-quarterly composure applied to a contractor's workbook.

This is a deliberate counter-positioning against the four traps that 'contractor software' snaps to: hi-vis construction-cliché, generic SaaS-cream, AI-startup purple-gradient, and consumer-cute. Every visual choice should read as 'a team of contractors-turned-builders made this for themselves,' not 'an agency themed a CRM in October.'

The system serves three scenes simultaneously: a contractor in direct sunlight on a jobsite, a contractor at a desk at 9pm finishing invoices, and a contractor standing next to a homeowner presenting an estimate. No choice is allowed that only works in one scene.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper background, dense black ink, restrained accent.
Hairline borders (0.5px) where most products use 1px. Lines whisper.
Geist as the single typeface; weight + size do all the hierarchy work.
Flat at rest. Elevation is a state, not a default.
The accent (Pressroom Indigo) is rare. Used ≤10% of any screen.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Pressroom Indigo appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. If two indigo elements compete on the same screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Warm-Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is tinted warm. #000 and #fff are prohibited as surface or text colors. The closest legal equivalents are Ink (#111113) and pure white only inside .paper-card.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Emerald, Rose, and Amber appear only when they encode state. They never decorate.

rules.name: The Single-Typeface Rule
rules.body: Geist does the entire hierarchy. Don't introduce a serif, script, or second sans. Hierarchy comes from scale, weight, and letter-spacing within the one family.

rules.name: The Tabular Numeric Rule
rules.body: Money, counts, dates, durations, percentages use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Mixed proportional and tabular numbers in the same column is forbidden.

rules.name: The Quiet-Caps Rule
rules.body: The quiet-caps style (11px, 500, +0.14em, uppercase, --ink-soft) is the system's section caption. Do not bump its size to make it more important.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat unless they are temporarily floating. The shadow vocabulary is exhaustive; anything not in it is invented and wrong.

rules.name: The Hairline-Beats-Border Rule
rules.body: Default to 0.5px hairlines. Use full 1px borders only when the element must remain legible on top of a colored surface. 2px+ borders are prohibited as decorative accents.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Card Rule
rules.body: Cards are not the default container. Use .paper-card only when the contained content is logically a discrete object that benefits from being lifted off the background.

rules.name: The Hairline-Is-The-Boundary Rule
rules.body: The 0.5px hairline (--ink-line) is how the system signals structure. Full borders, ruled lines, and shadow-only separators are wrong unless explicitly called for by a Component spec.

dos: Do use Pressroom Indigo (#4f46e5) sparingly: focus rings, primary links, active nav, ≤10% of any screen.
Do prefer hairline 0.5px borders (--ink-line) over full 1px borders.
Do use quiet-caps (11px, 500, +0.14em tracking, uppercase, --ink-soft) for every section caption, group label, and form label.
Do use tabular numerals for money, dates, durations, counts, percentages.
Do treat shadow as a state, not a style. Static elements are flat; elevation appears only when something temporarily lifts.
Do tint every neutral toward warm. --paper and --paper-deep are not pure gray for a reason.
Do keep body line length to 65–75ch.
Do ensure all mobile touch targets are ≥44px and contrast meets WCAG 2.2 AA, with sun-readability as an additional informal constraint.
donts: Don't use construction-cliché visuals: no hi-vis safety yellow, no hardhat icons, no hammer mascots, no blueprint backgrounds, no jobsite-photo heroes, no orange CTAs.
Don't drift toward generic SaaS-cream: no HubSpot blue, no identical card grids, no hero-metric template tiles, no marketing-template chrome bolted onto product UI.
Don't use AI-startup purple-gradients, sparkle icons on every AI feature, glassmorphism as default, or Linear-clone dark.
Don't use mascot illustrations, playful pastels, gamified streaks, or oversized emoji icons.
Don't use #000 or #fff as surface or text colors.
Don't introduce a second typeface. Geist is the entire system.
Don't use side-stripe borders greater than 1px as colored accents.
Don't reach for a modal as the first thought.
Don't invent a new accent color. Pressroom Indigo is the only accent.
Don't add md: / lg: / xl: Tailwind responsive variants in new mobile work.
Don't add dark-mode (.dark) variants in new work.
Don't introduce a token that doesn't already exist in globals.css or tailwind.config.ts.
